_about: New guide (2026-11-10, write-article), T3 of docs/plans/report-4-articles-2026-11.md: an 'AI gap' topic. Posts disagree on which states stop insurers dropping a home over roof age; 2026 headlines said Texas had 'just banned' it. This ledger holds only laws we read at the source on 2026-11-10. It does NOT claim the other states have no rule. No insurer is named anywhere.
question: Can my insurer refuse, cancel or not renew my home insurance because of the roof's age, and which states limit that?
verdictConfirmed: It depends on the state. Florida (since July 1, 2022) and Virginia (from January 1, 2027, asphalt shingle only) protect roofs under 15 years old and give older roofs an inspection route tied to 5 or more years of useful life; California adds an inspection rule from January 1, 2028; Texas, Maine and Minnesota bar decisions based on age alone (Texas names roofing) but allow condition.

facts.claim: Florida, Fla. Stat. 627.7011(5)(b) (The 2026 Florida Statutes): no refusal to issue or renew solely because of the age of a roof less than 15 years old.
facts.quote: An insurer may not refuse to issue or refuse to renew a homeowner's policy insuring a residential structure with a roof that is less than 15 years old solely because of the age of the roof.

facts.claim: Florida 627.7011(5)(c): for a roof at least 15 years old, the insurer must allow an inspection by an authorized inspector at the homeowner's expense before requiring replacement; no refusal solely because of roof age if the inspection indicates 5 years or more of useful life remaining.
facts.quote: For a roof that is at least 15 years old, an insurer must allow a homeowner to have a roof inspection performed by an authorized inspector at the homeowner's expense before requiring the replacement of the roof of a residential structure as a condition of issuing or renewing a homeowner's insurance policy. The insurer may not refuse to issue or refuse to renew a homeowner's insurance policy solely because of roof age if an inspection of the roof of the residential structure performed by an authorized inspector indicates that the roof has 5 years or more of useful life remaining.

facts.claim: Florida 627.7011(5)(d): roof age runs from the last date 100 percent of the surface was built or replaced to the code then in effect, or the initial date of a partial replacement when later partial work completed 100 percent.
facts.quote: a roof's age shall be calculated using the last date on which 100 percent of the roof's surface area was built or replaced in accordance with the building code in effect at that time or the initial date of a partial roof replacement when subsequent partial roof builds or replacements were completed that resulted in 100 percent of the roof's surface area being built or replaced.

facts.claim: Florida 627.7011(5)(e): applies to policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2022. (6)(b): does not apply to mobile home policies. (6)(c): does not limit rejecting or nonrenewing for other lawful reasons. Section history last amended s. 8, ch. 2024-182 (no 2026 change).
facts.quote: This subsection applies to homeowners' insurance policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2022. ... (6) This section does not: ... (b) Apply to mobile home policies. (c) Limit the ability of an insurer to reject or nonrenew any insured or applicant on the grounds that the structure does not meet underwriting criteria applicable to replacement cost or law and ordinance policies or for other lawful reasons.

facts.claim: Florida 627.7011(5)(a): 'authorized inspector' is an inspector approved by the insurer who is a licensed home inspector, certified building code inspector, licensed general/building/residential contractor or a roofing contractor, professional engineer, professional architect, or another individual or entity the insurer recognizes as qualified.
facts.quote: the term "authorized inspector" means an inspector who is approved by the insurer and who is: 1. A home inspector licensed under s. 468.8314; 2. A building code inspector certified under s. 468.607; 3. A general, building, or residential contractor licensed under s. 489.111 or a roofing contractor; 4. A professional engineer licensed under s. 471.015; 5. A professional architect licensed under s. 481.213; or 6. Any other individual or entity recognized by the insurer as possessing the necessary qualifications

facts.claim: Virginia 2026 Acts of Assembly, Chapter 657 (HB 677), approved April 13, 2026, amends Va. Code 38.2-2114 by adding subsection K; effective January 1, 2027. K: no refusing coverage, cancelling or refusing to renew an owner-occupied dwelling policy solely based on the age of the asphalt shingle roof (i) if less than 15 years old or (ii) without permitting the owner or purchaser to provide written proof of actual age; absent proof, the insurer must permit an inspection by an authorized inspector at the owner's or purchaser's expense.
facts.quote: No insurer shall refuse coverage or cancel or refuse to renew a policy written to insure an owner-occupied dwelling solely based on the age of the dwelling's asphalt shingle roof (i) if such asphalt shingle roof is less than 15 years old or (ii) without permitting the owner or purchaser of the dwelling to provide written proof of the actual age of the asphalt shingle roof. In the absence of such proof, the insurer shall permit a roof inspection performed by an authorized inspector at the owner's or purchaser's expense to determine the actual age of the asphalt shingle roof. ... 2. That the provisions of this act shall become effective on January 1, 2027.

facts.claim: Virginia 38.2-2114(K)(1): age is calculated from the last date 100 percent of the asphalt shingle roof surface was built or replaced to code, or the initial date of a partial replacement when later partial work completed 100 percent (same method as Florida).
facts.quote: the actual age of the asphalt shingle roof shall be calculated using (i) the last date on which 100 percent of the asphalt shingle roof's surface area was built or replaced in accordance with the building code in effect at such time or (ii) the initial date of a partial asphalt shingle roof replacement when subsequent partial asphalt shingle roof builds or replacements were completed that resulted in 100 percent of the asphalt shingle roof's surface area being built or replaced.

facts.claim: Virginia 38.2-2114(K)(2): no refusal, cancellation or nonrenewal solely based on the roof's condition if an authorized inspector reports 5 years or more of useful life; replacement can't then be a condition of issuing or renewing; for a roof at least 15 years old the insurer must permit an inspection at the owner's or purchaser's expense before requiring replacement; a 5-year finding does not stop the insurer requiring repair or replacement of damaged, deteriorated or deficient portions.
facts.quote: Notwithstanding the age of the asphalt shingle roof, no insurer shall refuse coverage or cancel or refuse to renew a policy written to insure an owner-occupied dwelling solely based on the condition of the dwelling's asphalt shingle roof if an authorized inspector reports that the asphalt shingle roof has five years or more of useful life remaining. If an authorized inspector reports that the asphalt shingle roof has five years or more of useful life remaining, replacement of the asphalt shingle roof shall not be required as a condition of issuing or renewing a policy to insure an owner-occupied dwelling. For a roof that is at least 15 years old, the insurer shall permit a roof inspection performed by an authorized inspector at the owner's or purchaser's expense before requiring the replacement of the roof as a condition of issuing or renewing a policy to insure an owner-occupied dwelling. A finding of five or more years of useful life shall not preclude an insurer from requiring repair or replacement of damaged, deteriorated, or deficient portions of a roof as noted in the inspection report.

facts.claim: Virginia 38.2-2114(K)(3): 'authorized inspector' means a licensed home inspector, a licensed contractor with a residential building classification, a professional engineer, or any other individual or entity the insurer recognizes as qualified. Unlike Florida's definition, it does not say the first three must be approved by the insurer.
facts.quote: "authorized inspector" means a home inspector licensed under Chapter 5 of Title 54.1 (§ 54.1-500 et seq.), a contractor with a residential building classification licensed under Chapter 11 of Title 54.1 (§ 54.1-1100 et seq.), a professional engineer, or any other individual or entity recognized by an insurer as possessing the necessary qualifications

facts.claim: Virginia 38.2-2114(K)(4): receipts or contracts from installation or replacement, building permits, or an authorized inspector's report estimating age or confirming 5+ years of life, provided by the owner or purchaser, are sufficiently determinative of age or condition.
facts.quote: copies of receipts or contracts from the initial roof installation or replacement, copies of building permits for installation or replacement, or a report from an authorized inspector estimating the age of the asphalt shingle roof or that the roof has five years or more of useful life remaining provided by the owner or purchaser shall be sufficiently determinative of the age or condition of the asphalt shingle roof.

facts.claim: Virginia 38.2-2114(K)(5)-(6): no duty to cover a roof with unrepaired damage, material defects, installation deficiencies, deterioration and similar conditions noted by an inspector (but once cured, no refusal solely on them); 'refuse coverage' means only the base policy; reductions in coverage, higher deductibles or removed endorsements must rest on specific, documented risk characteristics and not be imposed solely to avoid the section.
facts.quote: Nothing in subdivisions 1 through 4 shall be construed to require an insurer to issue, renew, or maintain coverage for any asphalt shingle roof that has unrepaired damage, material defects, installation deficiencies, deterioration, inadequate maintenance, structural concerns, moisture intrusion, or any other such condition as noted by an authorized inspector. ... provided that any reductions in coverage, increase in deductibles, or removal of endorsements shall be based on specific, documented risk characteristics of the insured property and shall not be imposed solely to avoid compliance with the requirements of this section.

facts.claim: Virginia 38.2-2114 (existing text, reenacted in ch. 657): notice of cancellation or nonrenewal must give a date at least 30 days after mailing and state the specific reason; within 10 days of receipt the insured may ask the Commissioner in writing to review; the policy stays in full force during the review except for nonpayment of premium. Subsection I ends: nothing in this section prohibits setting rates in accordance with relevant actuarial data.
facts.quote: which shall be at least 30 days after mailing or delivering to the named insured the notice of cancellation or refusal to renew ... State the specific reason for terminating the policy or contract ... Within 10 days of receipt of the notice of termination any insured or his attorney shall be entitled to request in writing to the Commissioner that he review the action of the insurer ... The policy shall remain in full force and effect during the pendency of the review by the Commissioner except where the cancellation or refusal to renew is for reason of nonpayment of premium ... Nothing in this section prohibits any insurer from setting rates in accordance with relevant actuarial data.

facts.claim: California SB 1301 (Allen): Chaptered by Secretary of State, Chapter 693, Statutes of 2026; approved by the Governor 09/27/26. Adds Insurance Code 676.14: beginning January 1, 2028, no refusing to issue or renew, or determine eligibility, solely on roof age if the policyholder obtains and pays for an independent inspection confirming at least five years of useful roof life; (b) the insurer may still take roof age into consideration; operative January 1, 2028.
facts.quote: Beginning January 1, 2028, an insurer shall not refuse to issue or renew, or determine eligibility for, a residential property insurance policy solely on the basis of the age of the roof if the policyholder obtains and pays for an independent inspection of the roof that confirms at least five years of useful roof life remaining. (b) This section does not prohibit an insurer from taking into consideration the age of the roof when issuing or renewing, or determining eligibility for, a residential property insurance policy. ... 09/27/26 Chaptered by Secretary of State. Chapter 693, Statutes of 2026. 09/27/26 Approved by the Governor.
facts.source: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billHistoryClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB1301 and billTextClient (read in the in-app browser; curl gets 403)

facts.claim: California Insurance Code 676.11 (SB 1301, operative January 1, 2028): an insurer that refuses to renew must give a detailed plain-language explanation and all nonaerial imagery relied on, and inspection findings on request; if the dispute concerns the property's condition, the policyholder may request an onsite physical inspection.
facts.quote: An insurer that refuses to renew a policy shall provide the policyholder with a detailed, plain language explanation of the grounds for the nonrenewal. An insurer shall also provide the policyholder with all nonaerial imagery relied upon as a basis for the decision ... If the dispute concerns the condition of the property, a policyholder may request that the insurer conduct an onsite physical inspection of the property ... This section shall become operative on January 1, 2028.
facts.source: Cal. Ins. Code 676.11 as added by SB 1301 (2026 ch. 693)

facts.claim: Texas, 28 TAC 21.1006, proposal issued September 29, 2026 (TDI, 211006proposal.pdf): TDI says the amendments clarify the existing prohibition and do not change the rule's meaning or application; (b) an insurer may not decline to write residential property insurance based on the age of the property or any of its components or materials, including wiring, heating, air conditioning, plumbing, siding, and roofing (siding newly added); (d) does not prohibit declining based on physical condition. Comments due 5:00 p.m. central November 9, 2026; public hearing November 3, 2026. Adoption not confirmed as of 2026-11-10.
facts.quote: The proposed amendments to §21.1006 clarify the existing prohibition against refusing to write or renew residential property insurance on the basis of the property's age. These amendments do not change the rule's meaning or application. ... (b) An insurer may not decline to write residential property insurance based on the age of: (1) the property; or (2) any of the property's individual components or materials, including wiring, heating, air conditioning, plumbing, siding, and roofing. ... (d) This section does not prohibit: (1) an insurer from declining to write coverage based on the physical condition of the property or any of the property's individual components or materials ... received by TDI no later than 5:00 p.m., central time, on November 9, 2026 ... public hearing under Docket No. 2874 at 2:00 p.m., central time, on November 3, 2026 ... Issued in Austin, Texas, on September 29, 2026.

facts.claim: TDI news release, September 29, 2026: TDI is clarifying its rule that insurers can't decline or not renew a home policy based on the age of a house or its roof; decisions may be based on physical conditions.
facts.quote: The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) is clarifying its rule that insurance companies can't decline or not renew a home insurance policy based on the age of a house or its roof. Under the rule, insurance companies may base decisions on the physical conditions of the home or its components, such as roofing, wiring, heating, air conditioning, plumbing, or siding.

facts.claim: Maine, 24-A M.R.S. 3057 (PL 2003, c. 671, Pt. A, §10): no cancelling or refusing to issue or renew a property policy solely on the basis of the age of the dwelling and without consideration of its current condition.
facts.quote: An insurance company authorized to transact business in this State may not cancel or refuse to issue or renew a property insurance policy subject to this subchapter solely on the basis of the age of the dwelling and without consideration of the current condition of the property. [PL 2003, c. 671, Pt. A, §10 (NEW).]

facts.claim: Minnesota 72A.20, subd. 13 (2026 Minnesota Statutes): refusing to renew or declining to offer or write homeowner's coverage solely because of the age of the primary structure is an unfair practice; (c) this does not prohibit rating standards based on the age of plumbing, electrical, heating or cooling, or other part of the structure whose age affects the risk of loss.
facts.quote: Refusing to renew, declining to offer or write, or charging differential rates for an equivalent amount of homeowner's insurance coverage ... solely because: ... (2) of the age of the primary structure sought to be insured; ... Paragraph (a), clause (2), shall not prohibit the use of rating standards based upon the age of the insured structure's plumbing, electrical, heating or cooling system or other part of the structure, the age of which affects the risk of loss.

facts.claim: Minnesota 65A.29 subd. 7: at least 60 days' advance notice of nonrenewal with the specific underwriting or other reason. Subd. 8(b): an insured may appeal any nonrenewal to the commissioner of commerce; the policy continues in force pending the appeal.
facts.quote: at least 60 days' advance notice of its intention. The notice must contain the specific underwriting or other reason or reasons for the indicated action ... an insured may appeal any nonrenewal under this section to the commissioner of commerce ... The insured's policy shall continue in force pending the conclusion of the appeal to the commissioner.
